source.pc: In this skill you learn to solve a quadratic equation when it is in its standard form . This includes determining the number of solutions, simplifying the square root (pulling out factors) and simplifying the resulting fraction. This skill does not include rewritten quadratic equations which still have to be brought to standard form first.

A quadratic equation is an equation of the form : it is a summation of a term with , a term with and a constant, without the presence of any higher powers of or any roots or similar. This type of equation can be solved by following a few fixed steps. Even if you don't understand why these steps work, following the procedure will get you to the right solutions.

Zero solutions
A quadratic equation doesn't always have two solutions though. Let's for instance study the equation . If we plot this, we get the following graph.

Note that this is the same parabola, except it's been shifted upwards by . Now it doesn't intersect with the -axis anymore! There are hence no solutions. There isn't a single number that exists for which .

We can see numerically why this is the case. Note that is always a positive number. After all, the square of a number is always positive. Similarly, is always positive. The only term in that may be negative is . However, this term will never match up to . As a result, the expression can never be zero.

So what happens if we still try to apply our general solution? In this case we have , and . Inserting this givesSimplifying this turns it intoNote that we now have a square root of a negative number. This is a mathematical impossibility: we cannot take square roots of negative numbers. Because our general solution gives a mathematical impossibility, there are no solutions possible to our equation.
In short: if the square root within the solution contains a negative number (so ) then the quadratic equation has no solutions.

There is an edge case where the quadratic equation has one solution. Let's consider for instance the equation . The corresponding graph is as follows.

You have seen that the number within the square root determines how many solutions the equation has. Because of this, this number is called the discriminant of the equation.

source.pc: Background: derivation of the quadratic formula

Though not needed for this skill, we can look at where the quadratic equation comes from. To be precise, we can derive it ourselves! It's fun to see this derivation some time, if only so you know why it's set up the way it is.

Our starting point is the quadratic equationFor reasons which will become clear later, we multiple all terms in this equation by to getWe also add and subtract to the equation to findThe reason why we did this, is because now we can pull the first three terms into a big square, likeNote that, if you expand the brackets, we come back to what we started with, so the equation is still valid. The next step is to bring the other terms to the right-hand side,Now we can cancel the square by taking the square root of both sides of the equation. When doing so, the rule says that we must also add a plus/minus symbol prior to the square root. So we getSubtracting and subsequently dividing by turns this intoWe have derived the quadratic formula, proving its correctness! Of course you could take the above steps every time you try to solve a quadratic equation, but simply inserting some numbers into the quadratic formula is a much easier way of solving quadratic equations.
